thesis_triggers.event: About 31% below spot and ~15% below the $297-304 July 2026 low, which already priced a 1.4% operating margin and negative FCF. It sits far enough under the ~$285 fundamental anchor that a sustained trade there would not be plain convergence to fair value. It would most likely mean the autonomy thesis is impaired: NHTSA forcing a Cybercab pause or a capped Part 555 exemption path, a serious robotaxi incident, or unsupervised expansion stalling. It could also mean core auto turned loss-making while >$25B/yr capex is funded with debt.

supervisor_summary: The five revised forecasts converge tightly: median ~$352-362, sigma ~0.5, fair values $280-295 on corrected share count and $2.17 2027 EPS, so TSLA carries a ~25% narrative premium over fundamentals. Checks this round settled only small points: merger odds are ~48% (not 74%) and two-sided in price effect; unsupervised robotaxi is still confined to TX/FL well short of the 12-state goal, and Q3 deliveries look down year on year. I keep the mean ladder with a ~0.5pp trim through the middle (P(>=372) = 0.457) and put the thesis break at ~$255, about 15% under the July low. Near-term swing factors are the Sept 30 NHTSA response, the Oct 2 deliveries print and Q3 earnings.
key_drivers: Valuation is mostly option value. At $1.47T on 3.95B shares, TSLA trades at ~171x 2027 consensus EPS of $2.17. The agents' fundamental anchors cluster at $280-295, ~23% below spot, but the market has kept a narrative premium (analyst mean $397, median $415).

Autonomy execution: ~200 unsupervised robotaxis in six TX/FL cities against Musk's ~12-state year-end target, and the NHTSA Special Order on Cybercab FMVSS 135 compliance (sworn answer due Sept 30), which could force a pause or a capped exemption path.
Cash burn and core auto: Q2 operating margin was 1.4%, FCF -$1.1B, 2026 capex >$25B and up to $30B of debt facilities. Q3 deliveries are tracking down YoY (~454-461k vs ~497k).
Delayed regulatory catalysts: the EU FSD vote is December at the earliest, with 7 of 27 states on board, and full China approval is still pending.
Tesla-SpaceX merger is a two-sided wildcard at ~48% before May 2027 on Kalshi.
